variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Private capital outpaces federal awards
variants.takeaway: The gap may partly reflect the dual-use nature of many Aus NatSec50 companies, which serve both commercial and government markets. However, it also points to the need for government to turn national security demand into procurement contracts that generate sustained revenue and help these companies scale.
variants.descriptor: Cumulative private capital raised and federal award value

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: The capital-to-awards gap widens
variants.takeaway: CDC’s large federal awards mask a wider gap across the rest of the cohort. Without CDC, private capital is 8.4 times federal award value, reinforcing the need to turn national security demand into sustained procurement revenue.
variants.descriptor: Cumulative private capital raised and federal award value

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Grants have faded as contracts recover
variants.takeaway: Grants fell from A$90.7 million in FY2023 to A$7.2 million in FY2026, so contract notices now make up more than nine-tenths of the cohort’s federal awards. Contract notices dipped to A$48.1 million in FY2025 before recovering to A$90.3 million.
variants.descriptor: Federal contract-notice and grant value by financial year (A$ millions)

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: CDC’s data-centre contracts drive the FY2025 peak
variants.takeaway: CDC’s A$252.0 million in FY2025 contract notices makes that year the highest shown, larger than the rest of the cohort’s combined awards in any year. Grants fell from A$90.7 million in FY2023 to A$7.2 million in FY2026.
variants.descriptor: Federal contract-notice and grant value by financial year (A$ millions)

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Defence anchors federal demand
variants.takeaway: Defence is the largest federal buyer in every year shown, with about four-fifths of award value in FY2024 and 68% in FY2026. Industry, Science & Resources ran a close second in FY2023 but has since fallen away.
variants.descriptor: Federal award value by buyer and financial year (A$ millions)

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Large awards reshape the federal buyer mix
variants.takeaway: Including CDC changes the FY2025 picture significantly: an A$226.2 million Services Australia contract makes that agency the largest buyer. In FY2026, CDC’s Home Affairs awards bring that agency almost level with Defence.
variants.descriptor: Federal award value by buyer and financial year (A$ millions)

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Equipment and software dominate procurement language
variants.takeaway: Equipment and software lead the vocabulary of contract titles, alongside research and support. The pattern points to a mix of technical products and supporting work rather than a single type of purchase.
variants.descriptor: Most frequent terms in federal contract-notice titles

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: CDC puts data infrastructure first in contract titles
variants.takeaway: Including CDC, “data” (150 titles) and “centre” (109) lead the vocabulary of contract notices, ahead of equipment (97) and software (60). Infrastructure-related work moves to the forefront of recorded procurement.
variants.descriptor: Most frequent terms in federal contract-notice titles

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Research leads federal procurement
variants.takeaway: Military science and research is the largest category by contract value, ahead of every other type of purchase. This shows companies are still proving their technologies to government rather than fielding them consistently.
variants.descriptor: Federal contract value by procurement category (A$ millions)

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Big-ticket deals overshadow a young defence-tech market
variants.takeaway: CDC’s engineering, data-services and property contracts are far larger than every other category. Beneath them, the categories closest to defence technology remain small and research-led, a sign of a sector still early in its relationship with federal buyers.
variants.descriptor: Federal contract value by procurement category (A$ millions)

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Electronic warfare and cyber outweigh their size in federal contracting
variants.takeaway: Electronic warfare has 3 of 49 companies but 44.5% of federal contract value, and advanced cyber 7 companies but 38.9%. Quantum technologies holds 44.8% of private capital yet only 7.1% of contract value, while 21 of 49 companies fall into none of the six recorded categories.
variants.descriptor: Number of companies, private-capital share and federal-contract share by AUKUS capability

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: CDC places most capital and contracts outside AUKUS categories
variants.takeaway: Including CDC, companies outside the six recorded AUKUS categories hold more than three-fifths of private capital and more than four-fifths of federal contract value while making up 22 of 50 companies. Among the tagged categories, quantum leads on capital and electronic warfare on contracts.
variants.descriptor: Number of companies, private-capital share and federal-contract share by AUKUS capability

variants.label: Original
variants.title: AI and autonomy lead recorded AUKUS representation
variants.takeaway: AI and autonomy is the most common recorded AUKUS capability, with 9 companies, followed by quantum technologies with 8 and advanced cyber with 7. More than two-fifths of the cohort (22 of 50 companies) falls outside these six categories, underscoring that AUKUS technology tags do not capture every company’s national security relevance.
variants.descriptor: Number of companies by recorded AUKUS technology area

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Quantum draws the most capital, autonomy the most awards
variants.takeaway: Quantum technologies holds the largest pool of private capital (A$2.9 billion) but only A$67.8 million in federal awards, while autonomy, robotics & sensing leads awards with A$354.3 million. Clean energy attracts A$242 million of private capital but only A$10.5 million in awards, showing a potential vulnerability for clean tech in the long run.
variants.descriptor: Companies, private capital and federal awards by critical technology area

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Information technologies lead capital and federal awards
variants.takeaway: Including CDC puts information and communications first on both financial measures. CDC alone accounts for about two-fifths of private capital and more than two-thirds of federal award value.
variants.descriptor: Companies, private capital and federal awards by critical technology area

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Quantum draws the most capital, autonomy the most awards
variants.takeaway: Quantum technologies holds the largest share of private capital (44.8%) but 8.7% of federal awards, while autonomy, robotics & sensing has the most companies and 45.3% of awards. Clean energy attracts 3.7% of private capital but only 1.3% of awards, showing a potential vulnerability for clean tech in the long run.
variants.descriptor: Company, private-capital and federal-award shares by critical technology area

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: Information technologies lead capital and federal awards
variants.takeaway: Including CDC puts information and communications first on both financial measures, with 47.9% of private capital and 79.0% of federal awards. CDC alone accounts for about two-fifths of private capital and more than two-thirds of federal award value.
variants.descriptor: Company, private-capital and federal-award shares by critical technology area

items.label: Technology verticals · companies, capital & federal awards

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Quantum draws the capital; cybersecurity wins the awards
variants.takeaway: Quantum technology has 6.1% of companies and 39.1% of private capital but only 3.8% of federal awards. Cybersecurity leads awards with 28.7%, ahead of space technology (20.1%), while robotics and drones has the most companies (16.3%).
variants.descriptor: Share of companies, private capital and federal awards by primary technology vertical

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: One company dominates both capital and awards
variants.takeaway: CDC accounts for about two-fifths of private capital and more than two-thirds of federal award value, lifting its technology, media and telecommunications vertical above every other vertical on both measures. Quantum ranks second on capital and cybersecurity on awards, while clean technology and space have far more companies but a fraction of the financial weight.
variants.descriptor: Share of companies, private capital and federal awards by primary technology vertical

variants.label: Excluding CDC
variants.title: Federal procurement is more concentrated than private capital
variants.takeaway: Federal contracts flow to a narrower group of companies than private capital. The ten largest contract recipients hold about four-fifths of contract value, against about two-thirds of capital for the ten largest fundraisers; PentenAmio leads contracts with 29.5% and PsiQuantum leads capital with 36.2%.
variants.descriptor: Share of private capital and federal contract value by company rank band (companies ranked separately on each measure)

variants.label: Including CDC
variants.title: CDC pushes procurement concentration higher still
variants.takeaway: With CDC included, CDC Data Centres holds 75.9% of federal contract value and 39.9% of private capital. The remaining 49 companies share less than a quarter of contract value between them.
variants.descriptor: Share of private capital and federal contract value by company rank band (companies ranked separately on each measure)

variants.label: Original
variants.title: Defence listings build momentum on the ASX
variants.takeaway: Three Australian defence technology companies listed on the ASX between May and September 2026, raising A$58 million between them. This run of recent IPOs points to growing public-market momentum for Australian defence, alongside private funding.
variants.descriptor: Selected Australian defence IPOs and capital raised

variants.label: Original
variants.title: 35 NatSec50 companies have recorded offices outside Australia
variants.takeaway: Just over half of the Australian NatSec50 companies have at least one office in the US, and more than a quarter have at least one office in the UK.
variants.descriptor: Companies with a recorded office presence by country

variants.label: Original
variants.title: New South Wales anchors the NatSec50
variants.takeaway: Almost half the cohort (23 companies) is headquartered in New South Wales, the largest concentration in the country. The ACT, South Australia, Victoria and Queensland provide additional centres of activity, including the Australian headquarters of US-based PsiQuantum (Brisbane) and Dtex Systems (Canberra).
variants.descriptor: Company headquarters by state and territory

variants.label: Original
variants.title: New South Wales leads a broader office network
variants.takeaway: The cohort’s office footprint extends beyond its headquarters, with substantial company presence in Victoria and the ACT alongside New South Wales. This points to several innovation hubs within Australia.
variants.descriptor: Companies with a recorded office presence by Australian state and territory

variants.label: Original
variants.title: The NatSec50 has an AUKUS-wide footprint
variants.takeaway: Recorded offices connect the cohort to all three AUKUS countries, with the US the more common overseas location. That presence provides an organisational link to partner markets, although it does not establish participation in AUKUS programmes.
variants.descriptor: Companies with a recorded office presence in AUKUS countries

variants.label: Original
variants.title: Employment growth has several leading contributors
variants.takeaway: PsiQuantum, Dtex Systems and Infravision together account for about a third of the cohort’s net recorded headcount gain. The ten companies shown account for 65% of the gain, with the rest spread across the other 40.
variants.descriptor: Top 10 companies by change in company-wide headcount, December 2022 to current 2026

variants.label: Original
variants.title: Workforce scale differs across technology areas
variants.takeaway: Autonomy and information technologies together employ nearly three-fifths of the recorded workforce. Quantum employment has more than doubled since December 2022, led by PsiQuantum, while information technologies and manufacturing & materials have each grown by about three-quarters.
variants.descriptor: Company-wide headcount by critical technology area, December 2022–current 2026

variants.label: Original
variants.title: The typical NatSec50 company has grown substantially
variants.takeaway: Median recorded headcount has more than doubled since December 2022 and is now more than four times the median across the wider eligible company pool. Growth in the typical company shows that the cohort’s expansion extends beyond its largest employers.
variants.descriptor: Median company-wide headcount, December 2022–current 2026

variants.label: Original
variants.title: NatSec50 employment outpaces the wider pool
variants.takeaway: NatSec50 headcount has grown 77.9% since December 2022, ahead of the wider eligible company pool’s 61.7%. The cohort’s share of recorded employment rose from 57.6% to 63.4%.
variants.descriptor: Growth in total company-wide headcount since December 2022 (%)

items.label: Companies with recorded US government work

variants.label: Original
variants.title: PsiQuantum accounts for most of the cohort’s US government work
variants.takeaway: Thirteen of the 50 companies have recorded US government work: 11 hold prime awards, and Silentium Defence and Skyborne Technologies appear only through subawards. PsiQuantum’s US$217.1 million, mostly from DARPA’s utility-scale quantum computing program, is almost two-thirds of the cohort’s recorded prime obligations, and for seven of the 11 prime awardees US obligations exceed their recorded Australian contract value.
variants.descriptor: Recorded US prime obligations and subawards by company (USD millions)

variants.label: Original
variants.title: DARPA dominates recorded US prime obligations
variants.takeaway: DARPA accounts for 63% of the cohort’s recorded US prime obligations, mostly through PsiQuantum’s US$183.8 million utility-scale quantum computing agreement, alongside awards to Q-CTRL, Diraq and Silicon Quantum Computing. The Office of the Secretary of Defense and the US Navy follow, largely through The Whiskey Project Group’s two Other Transaction agreements, while the US Air Force’s share comes almost entirely from PsiQuantum’s photonics contracts.
variants.descriptor: US prime obligations by awarding agency (USD millions)
